THE RULE, ONE PLACE: in src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py, every expression reaches sympy's gcd and lcm through wrappers carried in the locals both of _parse and of _domain_mismatch, built by one helper, so a pole base like 1/gcd(y - x, x - y) follows the same order as the value. One decorator on each mode runs the mode once as today and records every gcd or lcm call with two or more generators, read with sympy's own generator discovery (parallel_poly_from_expr; a non-polynomial generator such as sin(x) counts). With none recorded it returns that first result unchanged: no new step, detail or data for any other claim. With some recorded it computes each call's value under every ordering of the union of their generators and, when those values differ, runs the mode once more per distinct assignment of values, at an order that yields it. Every status equal: the first result stands, its detail adding that it held under all N variable orders. Otherwise it returns na(<the mode's check name>, reason), the reason saying the claim's reading rests on the variable order and naming the values the orders gave. Compared by status alone; orders are walked in a fixed sorted sequence, so a repeated claim gets a byte-identical response.

FORMS: the two-argument form, the sequence form (gcd((a, b, c)), gcd(Tuple(a, b)), lcm likewise) and nesting (gcd(gcd(a, b), c), a gcd inside any larger expression, gcd beside lcm) all go through the rule. A call that states its own generators positionally (gcd(a, b, x, y)) renames with its claim, is already name-free, and passes through unchanged. A call with keyword arguments or a Poly argument and two or more generators cannot be reordered safely, so its claim reads not checkable with a reason that says so. An error from sympy under any order is a differing status, never a verdict.

DEGREE: degree(p) with p a Poly of two or more generators and no generator named raises the same kind of refusal sympy already gives the plain expression, so it reads not checkable through the existing parse path, with a reason asking for a generator. degree(p, y) and a one-generator Poly stay as they are. degree(Poly(x**2 + y**3, x, y)) is a miss by design, since a Poly built with stated generators cannot be told apart afterwards; a test and MEASURED.md say so.

BOUNDS: more than 4 generators in the union (24 orders) reads not checkable without any further run, the reason naming the limit, and one named constant holds that limit. A mode called from inside a decorated mode runs once, with no second loop. The order and the record live in contextvars.ContextVar values, never module globals; a test runs two claims on two threads at once and each gets its own reading. Nothing is cached across claims.

EVERY MODE: equality, derivative, integral, limit, solve, inequality, calc_chain, numeric and system, meaning every function in mathematics.py whose body reaches _parse. An AST test fails on any verify_* function that calls _parse, directly or through a helper, without the decorator, and proves it can fail by running on a planted function. A table test holds at least one claim per mode that reaches an order-dependent value and whose verdict the rule changes; a mode where no claim can do that names why in the test, with its evidence, and the checker holds that reason hardest.

Measured by the lead on main at 82078d1 with sympy 1.14.0, calling the verifier functions directly: gcd(y - x, x - y) = x - y reads CONFIRMED and, renamed, MISMATCH, and lcm the reverse, so one verdict of each pair is false. The want under-describes the defect in four ways, and this run fixes what was measured: (1) the choice moves the rational SCALE as well as the sign: gcd(x/2 - y/3, x - 2*y/3) comes back as x - 2*y/3 or as -3*x/2 + y; (2) it reaches nested claims (gcd(y - x, x - y) + 1 = x - y + 1) and the tuple and keyword forms (gcd((y - x, x - y)), gcd(y - x, x - y, modulus=5)), and a two-argument wrapper would miss those; (3) it is not only gcd and lcm: degree(Poly(x**2 + y**3)) = 2 reads CONFIRMED and, renamed, MISMATCH, because degree reads a Poly's first generator, though sympy refuses the plain expression and asks for a generator; (4) the order is sympy's generator table (_sort_gens: x sorts before a), not alphabetical as the want says. THE RULE: a verdict stands only if it stands under every generator order; where orders disagree the claim reads not checkable (NOT_APPLICABLE, so the response reads INCOMPLETE with gap_at set), never HOLDS or BROKEN. No benchmark case or tier row holds a gcd or an lcm, so the benchmark must not move. A throwaway of the rule gave one verdict under five renames, a three-way cycle among them, for 20 claims; that is a planning note, not evidence for any criterion below. The lead's probes are outside the repo and prove nothing here.

THE RULE, ONE PLACE: in src/concordance/verifiers/mathematics.py, one helper builds the locals for _parse and for _domain_mismatch, and those locals carry wrappers for gcd, lcm, Poly and degree. A wrapper calls sympy's own function with the same arguments and returns its value unchanged, or raises what sympy raises; beside that it records a reason when the call is unbound, as defined below. One decorator on each mode clears the record, runs the mode, and returns that mode's result, the same object, when nothing was recorded. When something was recorded it returns na(<the mode's check name>, <reason>), whatever the mode returned. The record lives in a contextvars.ContextVar, never a module global, and a mode called from inside a decorated mode shares the outer record. No claim is run twice, and nothing is cached across claims.

UNBOUND, DEFINED: gcd or lcm is unbound when any argument is not a sympy Number. An argument that is iterable (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__) is read element by element, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are all covered. Every positional argument counts, so a generator written in the claim makes the call unbound, and a keyword argument changes nothing. Poly is unbound when no generator is named (no positional generator and no gens keyword) and generator discovery finds two or more; a Poly with named generators is bound, so a function fed by one, such as degree or diff, reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree is unbound when its argument is not a Poly, generator discovery finds two or more, and no generator is named by a symbol or an expression, a numeric index naming nothing. sqrt(2) and pi are not sympy Numbers, so gcd(sqrt(2), 2) is unbound. The reason says what the value would rest on and what would bind it, in words a reader can act on.

goal: Close three measured defects in the mathematics verifier, which share one root: a value the claim never bound. This closes the want gcd-lcm-sign-depends-on-symbol-names (LEDGER Concordance-V3 2026-11-03-restatement-audit 21) and goes past it, because checker-31's review of the first plan (line 3) found more. All measured on main at 82078d1 with sympy 1.14.0; src/ and deploy/ are identical at ec68d79, the commit the box runs. (A) FALSE HOLDS: sympy evaluates gcd and lcm of expressions as polynomials before a binder or a substitution sees them, so the value is wrong at integer points. Sum(gcd(k, 12), (k, 1, 4)) = 4 reads HOLDS and = 10 reads BROKEN, though the sum is 1+2+3+4 = 10; Product(gcd(k, 12), (k, 1, 4)) = 1 reads HOLDS (the product is 24); Subs(gcd(x, 12), x, 6) = 1 reads HOLDS (it is 6); Sum(lcm(k, 12), (k, 1, 3)) = 72 reads HOLDS (it is 36); the system claim gcd(x, 12) = 1 at x = 6 reads HOLDS. A bare gcd(x, x + 2) = 1 reads HOLDS, true of polynomials and false of integers (x = 2 gives 2), and nothing tells the reader which was meant. (B) NAME DEPENDENCE: a polynomial gcd or lcm is defined only up to a unit, and sympy picks the unit by its default generator order, which rests on the names (its own table in _sort_gens, where x sorts before a, not alphabetical as the want says). gcd(y - x, x - y) = x - y reads HOLDS and, renamed, BROKEN; lcm the reverse; the scale moves as well as the sign (gcd(x/2 - y/3, x - 2*y/3)); so do the nested, sequence and keyword forms. Poly and degree read the same order: degree(Poly(x**2 + y**3)) = 2, degree(x**2 + sin(x)**3) = 2 and diff(Poly(x**2 + y**3)) = 2*x each flip under a rename. (C) FALSE BROKEN: _domain_mismatch compares pole bases as written, so 1/(y + x) = 1/(x + y), 1/(x*y) = 1/(y*x), 1/(x - y) = -1/(y - x) and 1/(2*x) = (1/2)/x read BROKEN, and 1/simplify(y + x) = 1/(y + x) flips under a rename. THE DECISION: the first plan's 'a verdict stands if it stands under every generator order' is withdrawn. It needed re-runs, a cap, a data comparison and coefficient-domain logic, and it still left gcd(x, x + 2) = 1 reading HOLDS. Instead the verifier stops answering for a value nobody bound: a gcd or lcm with any argument that is not a number reads not checkable (NOT_APPLICABLE, so the response reads INCOMPLETE with gap_at set) in every mode, and so does a Poly or a degree that rests on default generators. Polynomial gcd claims become a named miss, and a mode that states its ring and generators and compares up to a unit is filed as a want. A miss stays a miss. No benchmark case or tier row reaches gcd or lcm through an expression (its gcd cases are integer packets), so the moat must not move.

UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named by a symbol or expression (a numeric index names nothing). INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit or Limit, is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. The reason says what the value would rest on and what would bind it, in words a reader can act on, and names the polynomial mode where that is the fix.

UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named by a symbol or expression (a numeric index names nothing). Modes system, limit and solve substitute a value too, so they parse their texts at binder depth one. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. The reason says what the value would rest on and what would bind it, in words a reader can act on, and names the polynomial mode where that is the fix.

UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named by a symbol or expression (a numeric index names nothing). INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit or Limit, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit, Limit, solve or solveset, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. POLES, step poles-exact, on the owner's word 'Rebuild it narrow' after poles-canonical blocked at line 42. THE PRINCIPLE: the pole compare can only lift a BROKEN, and only on proof. Anything it cannot prove keeps the base's reading, so its worst case is what main does today. _domain_mismatch stays as it is at the base, and no new refusal or 'not compared' answer exists. One new helper is asked only after the difference has read zero and _domain_mismatch has named a difference: if it proves the two sides have the same zeros, the claim reads as if no difference were named; otherwise the base's BROKEN stands. What the proof requires, in order, each failure ending the attempt and keeping the base's reading: (1) every pole base splits structurally into written factors, Mul arguments and the base of a positive integer power, with nothing expanded; a number among them must be a nonzero Rational. (2) EACH WHOLE SIDE, not only its pole bases, is read twice before anything is evaluated: the text's syntax tree is an ALLOW-LIST, a name, an integer, and only +, -, *, / and ** with an integer exponent, so a call, a %, the word mod, a decimal and anything else end the attempt; and the unevaluated value holds nothing but Add, Mul, an integer Pow, a Symbol or a Rational. So the proof runs only on a rational function with rational coefficients, written out, and neither a term that cancels nor a call that evaluates away can hide a pole from it. Every factor then builds as Poly(factor, *free symbols sorted, domain='QQ'), non-zero and within a named term bound read without expanding. (3) Factors compare by primitive part with sign fixed, and matched factors leave the compare, so a claim never pays for what already matches. (4) If nothing is left on either side, the zeros are the same. If one side has something left and the other nothing, the attempt ends with no factoring. (5) Otherwise only the unmatched factors go to factor_list over QQ, within one named budget of total degree PER CLAIM, set by measurement, and they prove sameness only if their irreducible factors match as sets. Every confirm in verify_equality reads this answer, the exact-decimal and stated-precision paths included, since they skip the pole guard at the base. _worked_equality skips its expand and its simplify for a value that is not a rational function of its free symbols or is over the term bound, and falls through to its plain detail. Cost is pinned by COUNTS, never by timing: a spy at factor_list itself counts what it receives, and a claim with a non-zero difference makes no factor_list call; a spy on expand counts the terms it RETURNS; a property test holds that a value under the term estimate returns at most that many terms. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit, Limit, solve or solveset, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. Modes system, limit and solve substitute a value too, so they parse their texts at binder depth one. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit, Limit, solve or solveset, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. Modes system, limit and solve substitute a value too, so they parse their texts at binder depth one. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. (1) THE PRINCIPLE: at a finite point sympy's two sides are read only for a form on an ALLOW-LIST, decided by structure before any limit runs; anything else reads not checkable, in every direction, whatever sympy would answer. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit, Limit, solve or solveset, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. Modes system, limit and solve substitute a value too, so they parse their texts at binder depth one. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. The reason says what the value would rest on and what would bind it, in words a reader can act on, and names the polynomial mode where that is the fix.

POLES, step poles-exact, on the owner's word 'Rebuild it narrow' after poles-canonical blocked at line 42. THE PRINCIPLE: the pole compare can only lift a BROKEN, and only on proof. Anything it cannot prove keeps the base's reading, so its worst case is what main does today. _domain_mismatch stays as it is at the base, and no new refusal or 'not compared' answer exists. One new helper is asked only after the difference has read zero and _domain_mismatch has named a difference: if it proves the two sides have the same zeros, the claim reads as if no difference were named; otherwise the base's BROKEN stands. What the proof requires, in order, each failure ending the attempt and keeping the base's reading: (1) every pole base splits structurally into written factors, Mul arguments and the base of a positive integer power, with nothing expanded; a number among them must be a nonzero Rational. (2) EACH WHOLE SIDE, not only its pole bases, is read twice before anything is evaluated: the text's syntax tree is an ALLOW-LIST, a name, an integer, a unary sign, and only +, -, *, / and ** with an integer exponent, so a call, a %, the word mod, a decimal and anything else end the attempt; and the unevaluated value holds nothing but Add, Mul, an integer Pow, a Symbol or a Rational. So the proof runs only on a rational function with rational coefficients, written out, and neither a term that cancels nor a call that evaluates away can hide a pole from it. Every factor then builds as Poly(factor, *free symbols sorted, domain='QQ'), non-zero and within a named term bound read without expanding. (3) Factors compare by primitive part with sign fixed, and matched factors leave the compare, so a claim never pays for what already matches. (4) If nothing is left on either side, the zeros are the same. If one side has something left and the other nothing, the attempt ends with no factoring. (5) Otherwise each side's unmatched factors are multiplied out sparsely, in sympy's sparse polynomial ring and never as a dense Poly, whose cost grows with the degree in every symbol, within the term bound read before the multiplication runs, and the two products must be one polynomial up to a nonzero rational. A product has exactly the zeros of its factors, so equal products prove the two sides' zeros equal. This is a check and not a search: factor_list is called nowhere in this compare, and no degree budget exists. Every confirm in verify_equality reads this answer, the exact-decimal and stated-precision paths included, since they skip the pole guard at the base. _worked_equality skips its expand and its simplify for a value that is not a rational function of its free symbols or is over the term bound, and falls through to its plain detail. THE POLYNOMIAL MODE, step number-theory: a claim states gcd or lcm as a list of two or more polynomial texts, claimed_gcd or claimed_lcm as a text, generators as a list of names and ring as 'ZZ' or 'QQ'. mode polynomial routes to a helper polynomial_claim that requires all of them, and verify_number_theory delegates to it when a spec holds generators or ring, so a MATH_VERIFY packet reaches it too. Texts read through _parse with rational=True, each built as Poly(text, *generators, domain=ring), folded with Poly.gcd or Poly.lcm. Two polynomials are the same answer when they differ by a unit: plus or minus one over ZZ, any nonzero rational over QQ; zero equals only zero. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit, Limit, solve or solveset, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. Modes system, limit and solve substitute a value too, so they parse their texts at binder depth one. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. The reason says what the value would rest on and what would bind it, in words a reader can act on, and names the polynomial mode where that is the fix.

THE POLYNOMIAL MODE, step number-theory: a claim states gcd or lcm as a list of two or more polynomial texts, claimed_gcd or claimed_lcm as a text, generators as a list of names and ring as 'ZZ' or 'QQ'. mode polynomial routes to a helper polynomial_claim that requires all of them, and verify_number_theory delegates to it when a spec holds generators or ring, so a MATH_VERIFY packet reaches it too. Texts read through _parse with rational=True, each built as Poly(text, *generators, domain=ring), folded with Poly.gcd or Poly.lcm. Two polynomials are the same answer when they differ by a unit: plus or minus one over ZZ, any nonzero rational over QQ; zero equals only zero. Every symbol must be a named generator, so no symbol reaches a coefficient domain and nothing reads sympy's order. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. INSIDE A BINDER: degree or Poly with a free symbol, read inside an argument of Sum, summation, Product, product, Subs, limit, Limit, solve or solveset, or of integrate or Integral given limits in any written form, (x, 0, 2), Tuple(x, 0, 2) or (x, 2), is unbound, because it evaluates before the binder substitutes a value. diff and an indefinite integrate substitute nothing, so they are not binders here. Modes system, limit and solve substitute a value too, so they parse their texts at binder depth one. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. The reason says what the value would rest on and what would bind it, in words a reader can act on, and names the polynomial mode where that is the fix.

UNBOUND, DEFINED. gcd or lcm: every argument is flattened element by element (sympy's own test, hasattr __iter__, so a tuple, Tuple and FiniteSet are covered); the call is unbound if any element is not an exact rational (is_Rational), so a symbol, a Float, sqrt(2) and pi are all unbound. A bound call is the fold of sympy's two-argument function over the flattened elements, so no number is ever read as a generator. An empty sequence is refused, a single positional argument stays refused as sympy refuses it, and a sequence of one element reads as that element's absolute value, so a fold never keeps a sign. Poly: unbound when no generator is named and generator discovery finds two or more. A Poly with named generators is bound, and a function fed by one reads the claim's own order and renames with it. degree: unbound when its argument is not a Poly, discovery finds two or more generators, and none is named. A generator is named by a symbol, or by an expression generator discovery finds in the argument; a number, a boolean, a sequence, a set and any other expression name nothing. Poly reads a sequence of those as its generators, so Poly(x**2 + y**3, (x, y)) is bound and Poly(x**2 + y**3, FiniteSet(x, y)) is not. The reader counts binder depth; it does not work out which symbol is bound, so a claim whose inner symbol is not the binder's is a named miss. WHAT THE CODE SAYS, at HEAD 5cc7058, and src/concordance/mcp/server.py, transparency.py and http_api.py are the path: GET /seals (http_api.py, the /seals branch) reads ledger.list_precedents only and never touches attest, so a seal on that list says nothing about its log entry. GET /s/<hash>, with or without html=1, and GET /seal?hash= all call seal_fetch, and seal_fetch calls transparency.attest(h) (mcp/server.py:216) whenever the issuer key is configured. attest returns untouched only when a sidecar holds a settled log entry. Otherwise, with CONCORDANCE_PUBLISH on, it posts to Rekor and writes the sidecar on the box. /capabilities reads issuer_key_configured True and publish_by_default True. attest( appears nowhere else in src, so sealing does not log; docs/RUNBOOK.md line 16 says the same, the seal is logged at first fetch, with tools/publish_seals.py to flush what is pending ('cron it'), and nothing in deploy/ installs that.
SO THE GET HAS ONE OF TWO EFFECTS, and no public GET on this host can say which, since each read of the page is the same call. If 1ac55c15 has a settled sidecar, because its sealer fetched cite_url or a flush ran, the GET writes nothing. If it does not, the GET of a checker mints an envelope, puts a permanent entry on the public Rekor log, which cannot be undone, and writes a file on the box.
